title: Walsingham's cipher enclosure to John Somer, 21 July 1581

documents.shelfmark: TNA SP 53/11 no. 50I, folio 138 (DECODE R3839; R3840 is the neighbouring extracts)
documents.route: intercepted in a letter of Mary, Queen of Scots; sent by Walsingham to John Somer(s) 21 July 1581

plaintext.source: Biermann and Lasry's 2023 solution, published by Tomokiyo on 16 Sept 2026 (cryptiana mary3.htm): opening and glyph key only; some symbols unidentified

transcription.source: Tomokiyo's glyph-label transcription SP53_11_50b.txt (cryptiana), checked against DECODE R3839 image 3 (f. 138)

prior_solution.where: Solved by Norbert Biermann and George Lasry (2023); published by Satoshi Tomokiyo, cryptiana mary3.htm, 16 Sept 2026

conditions.human_role: Selected the target; supplied the DECODE login.

solution.what: Located Tomokiyo's 16 September 2026 publication of Biermann and Lasry's 2023 solution and verified its opening and key against the manuscript.

Compared key to manuscript and attempted numeric-label alignment and language-model solving. French 5-gram homophonic annealing (48 restarts x 10M) and English passes gave nonsense; no label-to-glyph concordance could be fixed from the short published opening.

outcome.method_basis: Biermann and Lasry solved the cipher in 2023 (published by Tomokiyo 16 Sept 2026); this work only located and checked the published opening and key against the manuscript.
outcome.notes: Not a new solve. Published glyph key lacks a numeric-label concordance and leaves some signs unknown. Tracker should be corrected to remove Portugal/French attribution from the distinct L'Abbadia worksheet. Verified opening: "The beirar is domestik servand to the erle of shrevisbvry". fraction_read ~0.09 = share represented by the published ten-word opening (approximate). Identified the enclosure (R3839 f. 138) and separated it from the L'Abbadia material; checked the published opening; no extension.

system.summary: Graphic-sign cipher with letter signs, whole-word signs and nulls (Biermann-Lasry key as published by Tomokiyo).
